title: WRAP up your backlog with GitHub Copilot coding agent - The GitHub Blog

facts.fact: The GitHub Blog article 'WRAP up your backlog with GitHub Copilot coding agent' was published on December 26, 2025.
According to GitHub's engineers, they have been using GitHub Copilot coding agent for over a year.
facts.quote: Engineers at GitHub have been using GitHub Copilot coding agent for over a year now

facts.fact: GitHub's WRAP acronym, which the article presents as a set of guidance for using Copilot coding agent, has four steps: Write effective issues, Refine your instructions, Atomic tasks, and Pair with the coding agent.
facts.quote: we have developed a handy acronym: WRAP, which stands for:

facts.fact: According to GitHub, coding agent custom agents are created from a natural language text file and can be applied at the enterprise, organization, or repository level.
facts.quote: coding agent custom agents can be created with a natural language text file, and are applicable at either the enterprise, organization, or repository level.

facts.fact: GitHub states that organization custom instructions for Copilot apply to all repositories in an organization.
facts.quote: you can also create a set of GitHub Copilot custom instructions for your entire organization.

facts.fact: GitHub states that repository custom instructions for Copilot apply to a single repository and that adding to them over time improves all Copilot responses in that repository.
facts.quote: Adding to these instructions over time will improve all the responses from any interactions with GitHub Copilot in that repository.
